en.name: Clip - Vision
en.description: CLIP connects images and text in the same “language.” It lets you search for images by typing words, or describe an image and find related content instantly.
en.long_description: CLIP is an AI model created to understand pictures and text together. It learns how to match what it “sees” in an image with the words we use to describe it. This makes it powerful for tasks like searching for photos using natural language (e.g. “a dog playing frisbee”), automatically tagging images with meaningful labels, or finding pictures similar to a description. Instead of relying on fixed categories, CLIP understands concepts more flexibly — closer to how people think about visuals and words.

en.name: Granite - Nano
en.description: The smallest and fastest model we ship, and still multilingual.
en.long_description:
The 97M-parameter member of IBM's Granite Embedding R2 family.

- 93 MB on disk and roughly three times faster per passage than anything else here.
- Emits 384-dimensional vectors, halving the storage an index needs compared with a 768-dimensional model.
- Keeps most of the cross-language strength of its larger sibling.
- Reads up to 32,768 tokens per passage.
- Ranks below the larger models on retrieval accuracy, which is the trade you are making.

Needs no query or passage prefix. Pick this one for mobile, for very large indexes, or wherever indexing throughput is the constraint.

en.name: Qwen - Instruct
en.description: Instruction-tuned retrieval across 100+ languages and code, with a very long context.
en.long_description:
Qwen3-Embedding is the highest scoring open embedding family on the multilingual MTEB leaderboard. This is the 0.6B member, quantised to run locally.

- Joint top of our retrieval benchmark alongside Harrier.
- Reads up to 32,768 tokens per passage, sixteen times the Gemma model.
- Covers natural language and source code in one vector space.
- Emits 1,024-dimensional vectors, so an index built on it is wider and more expensive to store than a 768-dimensional one.

The query side is prefixed with a retrieval instruction automatically. Pick this one for the best all-round accuracy when you can afford the index width.

en.name: Granite - Multilingual
en.description: The strongest choice when questions and answers are in different languages.
en.long_description:
IBM's Granite Embedding R2, covering more than 200 languages with focused support for 52 of them plus source code.

- By a wide margin the best model here at matching a question in one language to its answer in another. In our testing it scored 0.89 where GTE Multilingual scored 0.67.
- Reads up to 32,768 tokens per passage.
- Emits 768-dimensional vectors, so it drops into an existing GTE index without rebuilding at a new width.
- 298 MB on disk.

Needs no query or passage prefix. Pick this one for a knowledge base your team searches in several languages.

en.name: Nomic - Vision 1.5
en.description: Nomic Embed creates powerful fingerprints of images and text, placing them in the same space so you can instantly search, compare, or organize content by meaning instead of exact words.
en.long_description: Nomic Embed is a modern AI model designed to understand both images and text in a unified way. It doesn’t just look at pictures or words literally—it captures their meaning and places them on the same map. This means you can type a phrase like “a cozy living room” and quickly find matching photos, or group together similar items without predefined tags. It’s especially useful for organizing large collections of media, making recommendations, or building smarter search features that feel natural and intuitive.

en.name: GTE Multilingual
en.description: Strong multilingual model for local inference.
en.long_description:
The gte-multilingual-base model is the latest in the GTE (General Text Embedding) family of models, featuring several key attributes:

- High Performance: Achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) results in multilingual retrieval tasks and multi-task representation model evaluations when compared to models of similar size.
- Training Architecture: Trained using an encoder-only transformers architecture, resulting in a smaller model size. Unlike previous models based on decode-only LLM architecture (e.g., gte-qwen2-1.5b-instruct), this model has lower hardware requirements for inference, offering a 10x increase in inference speed.
- Long Context: Supports text lengths up to 8192 tokens.
- Multilingual Capability: Supports over 70 languages.
- Elastic Dense Embedding: Support elastic output dense representation while maintaining the effectiveness of downstream tasks, which significantly reduces storage costs and improves execution efficiency.
- Sparse Vectors: In addition to dense representations, it can also generate sparse vectors.

en.name: Gemma - Compact
en.description: Small, fast and multilingual. The best quality per megabyte we ship.
en.long_description:
EmbeddingGemma is Google's 300M-parameter multilingual embedding model, built on Gemma 3 and trained across more than 100 languages.

- Smallest capable option: 188 MB on disk, so it suits laptops and mobile devices.
- Matches models five times its size on retrieval quality in our own testing.
- Produces 768-dimensional vectors, the same width as GTE Multilingual, so it is a drop-in replacement for an existing index of that size.
- Trades context for size: it reads up to 2,048 tokens per passage, where the other models here read far more.

Pick this one when index size and speed matter and your passages are short.

en.name: E5 Large v2
en.description: Hosted English text embeddings for query and passage retrieval. Returns 1,024-dimensional vectors with a 512-token input limit.
en.long_description: Hosted English text embeddings for query and passage retrieval. Returns 1,024-dimensional vectors with a 512-token input limit. Flow-Like applies the model’s query and document prefixes before sending text to the hosted server.

en.name: Harrier - Precision
en.description: Microsoft's retrieval model. Strongest on English, at the cost of size.
en.long_description:
Harrier is Microsoft's open embedding model, released under the MIT licence.

- Joint top of our retrieval benchmark alongside Qwen.
- Reads up to 32,768 tokens per passage and emits 1,024-dimensional vectors.
- Strongest of everything we tested at ranking English passages.
- Weakest of the multilingual options at matching a question in one language to an answer in another, so it is a poor fit for a mixed-language index.
- The largest bit here at 1.3 GB.

The query side is prefixed with a retrieval instruction automatically. Pick this one for English-first search where accuracy outranks download size.
